articles.title: The browser wars aren't about search anymore — here are the best alternatives to Chrome and Safari | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The browser wars have entered a new phase this year: The fight isn’t just over search results anymore — it’s over which company’s AI gets to act on your behalf inside the browser. Google Chrome and Apple’s Safari still dominate the market overall, with Chrome’s edge coming largely from how aggressively it has woven generative AI into search. But 2026 has brought a wave of new entrants — from well-funded startups to Big Tech — all betting that the browser is about to become less like a window onto the web and more like an assistant that gets things done for you.
Users looking for alternatives to Chrome and Safari can choose from a growing variety of browsers aimed at challenging the industry giants. To help navigate the competitive landscape, we’ve compiled an overview of some of the top alternative browsers available today. This includes browsers leveraging AI, open source browsers that promote customization and privacy, and “mindful browsers” — a new term that refers to browsers designed to enhance user well-being.
AI-powered browsers
Perplexity’s Comet
Perplexity launched its AI-powered web browser in July 2025. Called Comet, the company’s new product acts as a chatbot-based search engine and can perform actions like summarizing emails, browsing web pages, and performing tasks such as sending calendar invites. It’s currently only available to users with Perplexity’s $200/month Max plan, but there’s also a waitlist where people can sign up.
The Browser Company’s Dia
The Browser Company, the startup behind the Arc browser, introduced Dia last summer. The AI-centric browser looks similar to Google Chrome but has an AI chat tool.
Dia is designed to help users navigate the web more easily. It’s able to look at every website that a user has visited and every website they’re logged into, enabling it to help you find information and perform tasks. For instance, Dia can provide information about the page a user is currently browsing, answer questions about a product, and summarize uploaded files.
Dia is currently free to download.
Opera’s Neon
Opera entered the AI agentic browser war in May 2025 with Neon, which has contextual awareness and can do things like researching, shopping, and writing snippets of code. Notably, it can even perform tasks while the user is offline.
Neon is currently available on macOS and Windows. The subscription costs $19.90 per month.
OpenAI’s Atlas (killed July 2026)
Last October, OpenAI launched its AI-powered web browser, called Atlas. The browser allowed users to ask ChatGPT about search results and browse websites within the chatbot instead of being directed to outside links. There was also an “agent mode” for users to ask ChatGPT to complete tasks on their behalf.
However, the company recently decided to shut down the browser and instead incorporate some of the agentic browsing capabilities into ChatGPT’s desktop app and Chrome extension.
Aside
Backed by Y Combinator, Aside is an AI-first, browser-native automation platform built to autonomously complete tasks, fill out forms, and manage data on behalf of users. The company describes the experience simply: “Give it your passwords, browsing history, and browser context.” Unlike traditional automation tools that rely on integrations, Aside operates directly within the browser itself, allowing it to work across Gmail, Notion, Slack, Figma, and banking platforms.
Jatter
Jatter launched its AI-powered browser in June, giving users the ability to ask questions about any web page, uncover relevant insights, and receive personalized recommendations based on their browsing activity. Additionally, Jatter offers an integrated Notes app, so it can learn from that content, summarize notes, and surface key details.
Jatter is currently available on Mac, Windows, iOS, and Android devices. It’s free to use, but there’s an optional subscription for $10 per month.
Privacy-focused browsers
Brave
Brave is among the more well-known privacy-first browsers, popular for its built-in ad and tracker blocking capabilities. It also has a gamified approach to browsing, rewarding users with its own cryptocurrency called Basic Attention Token (BAT). When users choose to opt in to view ads, supporting their favorite websites, they get a share of the ad revenue. Additional features include a VPN service, an AI assistant, and a video calling feature.
DuckDuckGo
DuckDuckGo is another browser that many people are probably already familiar with, thanks to its search engine by the same name. Launched in 2008, the company recently made significant investments in its browser to stay competitive by introducing generative AI features, such as a chatbot. It also enhanced its scam blocker to detect a wider range of scams, including fake cryptocurrency exchanges, scareware tactics, and fraudulent e-commerce websites. In addition to blocking scams, DuckDuckGo prevents trackers and ads, and it doesn’t track user data, resulting in fewer pop-ups for users.
Ladybird
Ladybird, led by GitHub co-founder and former CEO Chris Wanstrath, has an ambitious mission compared to rivals — it aims to build an entirely new open source browser from scratch. This means it will not rely on code from existing browsers, a feat that has rarely been accomplished. Most alternative web browsers depend on the Chromium open source project maintained by Google, which is the most widely used base for many browsers.
Like other privacy-focused browsers, Ladybird will offer features to minimize data collection, such as a built-in ad blocker and the ability to block third-party cookies. The browser has yet to be launched, with an alpha version scheduled for release this year for early adopters, available on Linux and macOS.
Vivaldi
Vivaldi is a Chromium-based browser created by one of the original developers of the Opera browser. Its biggest selling point is its customizable user interface, which allows users to change the appearance and enable or disable features. One unique feature is that the browser window changes color to match the website being viewed. Other key features include ad blocking, a password manager, no user data tracking, and productivity tools such as a calendar and notes.
Niche browsers
Opera Air
Opera launched the Air browser in February 2025, becoming one of the first mindfulness-themed browsers in the space. While Opera Air functions like a typical web browser, it includes unique features designed to support mental well-being. These features consist of break reminders and breathing exercises. Another feature, called “Boosts,” provides a selection of binaural beats to either help improve focus or relaxation.
SigmaOS
SigmaOS is a Mac-only browser featuring a workspace-style interface that emphasizes productivity. It displays tabs vertically, allowing users to treat them like a to-do list that can be marked as complete or snoozed for later. Users can create workspaces — essentially groups of tabs — to better organize different activities, such as separating work from entertainment.
This Y Combinator-backed browser has been around for a few years now and has introduced more AI features, including the ability to summarize various elements of a web page, such as ratings, reviews, and prices. It also has an AI assistant that can answer questions, translate text, and rewrite content.
SigmaOS is free to use, but users who want more than three workspaces can subscribe to a plan for $8 per month, which provides unlimited workspaces.
Zen Browser
Zen Browser aims to create a “calmer internet” with its open source browser. Zen lets users organize tabs into Workspaces, and offers Split View to view two tabs side by side, among other productivity-focused features. Users can also enhance their browsing experience with community-made plug-ins and themes, such as a mod that makes the tab background transparent.
This story has been updated after publication to include newly launched browsers.

articles.title: Startup news and updates: daily roundup (July 22, 2026)
articles.text:
Startup news and updates: Daily roundup (July 22, 2026)
YourStory presents the daily news roundup from the Indian startup ecosystem and beyond. Here's the roundup for Wednesday, July 22, 2026
YourStory brings you today’s headlines with the latest developments across sectors.
Funding news
Bioscan Research raises $1M in seed round
Medtech startup Bioscan Research has raised $1 million in a seed funding round led by Unicorn India Ventures to scale its non-invasive brain injury detection technology.
The startup said the capital will be used to expand into new markets, secure additional regulatory approvals, upgrade its flagship product, and develop new intellectual property.
Founded in 2017 by Anupam Lavania and Shilpa Malik, Bioscan Research develops affordable medical devices that combine optics, electronics, mechanics, software, and machine learning to enable the early detection of traumatic brain injuries. Its flagship product, CEREBO, uses near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and artificial intelligence to help detect intracranial injuries, even in patients who show no visible symptoms, enabling clinicians to intervene during the critical treatment window.
Other news
EduFund launches Vittam for MFDs and IFAs
EduFund has launched Vittam, a financial distribution platform designed for mutual fund sistributors and independent financial advisors.
Co-founded by Eela Dubey and Arindam Sengupta, with the mission of helping Indian families save and plan for their children's education, EduFund has, over the past six-and-a-half years, evolved into a comprehensive financial platform serving more than 300,000 families.
As households move through different life stages, their financial priorities expand beyond education to include investments, loans, insurance, retirement planning, and global opportunities.
Through Vittam, EduFund aims to equip MFDs and IFAs with an integrated platform that enables them to guide families across these evolving financial needs, while offering a suite of solutions that supports every stage of their financial journey.
Social Alpha launches clean energy acceleration programme
Social Alpha has launched Techtonic: Innovations in Clean Energy, a 12-month acceleration programme to support science-led startups developing solutions in energy access, energy storage, and energy efficiency.
The initiative, launched in partnership with Atal Innovation Mission, NITI Aayog, SELCO Foundation, Tata Power, Jakson Green, and Sagacity, will provide selected startups with grant funding, incubation support, pilot opportunities, market access, and potential seed investment, subject to due diligence.
The programme will support startups across different stages of growth. Early-stage ventures at the R&D stage (Technology Readiness Levels 3-4) can receive incubation support of up to Rs 10 lakh to advance prototype development, while growth-stage startups (TRL 7-9) will be eligible for support of up to Rs 60 lakh to accelerate commercial deployment, expand into new markets, and strengthen their business models.
Groww Foundation backs 35 young innovators at IIT Bombay
Groww Foundation, the philanthropic arm of Groww, has announced the inaugural cohort of its INV.ENT programme, selecting 19 ideas from 35 student innovators at the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Bombay. Chosen from nearly 400 submissions, the projects span AI, climate tech, robotics, defence, assistive technology, and social innovation.
Among the selected ideas are a digital marketplace connecting Dharavi's pottery artisans with customers, a wearable sleeve that guides physiotherapy patients through rehabilitation exercises, a platform that converts carbon dioxide into edible protein, and an AI-powered system designed to protect critical infrastructure from rogue drones.
The first cohort is divided into two tracks. Three student teams have been named Grand Challenge Fellows and are eligible for milestone-based funding of up to Rs 25 lakh annually. The remaining 16 teams will receive proof-of-concept grants of Rs 30,000 each to validate and develop their ideas.
Beyond funding, participants will gain access to mentorship and the 15,000 sq ft Groww Innovation Space at IIT Bombay's Desai Sethi School of Entrepreneurship (DSSE).
Grahaa Space completes Mission SIDDHI
Spacetech startup Grahaa Space has announced the successful completion of Mission SIDDHI, with its technology demonstration nanosatellite SOLARAS achieving all planned objectives in low Earth orbit (LEO).
The satellite successfully transmitted telemetry signals confirming the health of its onboard systems. The signals were received and verified by the SSPACE-Tarang ground station at the Indian Institute of Space Science and Technology (IIST), Thiruvananthapuram, while multiple amateur ground stations worldwide also tracked and received the transmissions across successive orbital passes.
Mission SIDDHI validated Grahaa Space's indigenously developed, stackable nanosatellite bus and platform, along with its onboard systems and subsystems, under real-world space conditions. The satellite also successfully transmitted payload data, marking a key milestone in the company's efforts to build reliable and scalable Earth observation nanosatellite technologies.
IIT Madras to host Digital India RISC-V Symposium 2026 on semiconductor innovation
The Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Madras, in partnership with the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY) and RISC-V International, will host the third Digital India RISC-V (DIR-V) Symposium 2026 on August 1-2 at the IIT Madras Research Park in Chennai.
Centred on the theme "Empowering Bharat's Semiconductor Future," the symposium aims to bring together policymakers, researchers, startups, industry leaders, investors, faculty members, and students to accelerate India's ambitions of becoming a global hub for semiconductor design, electronics manufacturing, and secure digital infrastructure.
The event will focus on indigenous processor technologies, secure computing systems, hardware innovation, artificial intelligence, and the rapidly expanding RISC-V ecosystem.
Kobie opens AI-focused tech hub in Bengaluru
Loyalty technology company Kobie has launched a new technology hub in Bengaluru to strengthen its AI-led product strategy and support global business growth. The India team has expanded to around 50 professionals and is hiring across software engineering, data science, cloud engineering, AI engineering, MLOps, AI governance and product development.
The company said artificial intelligence is now integrated across every layer of its technology organisation, enabling it to develop intelligent loyalty solutions for Fortune 500 clients. The Bengaluru hub will drive innovation in personalised customer engagement, predictive analytics and loyalty measurement while embedding governance, security and ethical AI practices into product development. Kobie said the investment will help clients improve customer loyalty and long-term enterprise value.
Citizens Financial appoints Rajesh Mani to lead India GCC
Citizens Financial Group has appointed Rajesh Mani as Managing Director of its India Global Capability Center (CFG India). Mani brings over two decades of experience in financial services and technology, most recently serving as Head of Asia Pacific Tech Hubs at Mastercard, where he led globally distributed technology teams. In his new role, he will oversee the expansion of CFG India by strengthening talent, enhancing organisational capabilities and driving closer collaboration with Citizens teams in the United States and global technology partners.
Citizens said its India GCC plays a critical role in advancing the bank's long-term strategy of building a more modern, resilient and technology-driven financial institution serving millions of customers across the US.
Plant.Digital partners Quest Global for industrial AI solutions
Plant.Digital has partnered with engineering services company Quest Global to accelerate the deployment of industrial digital solutions aimed at improving asset performance, operational efficiency and reliability. The collaboration will combine Plant.Digital's industrial expertise with Quest Global's engineering and digital transformation capabilities to deliver faster value for clients across the global energy sector. The companies will also support Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 by developing local talent, competency frameworks and long-term digital capabilities within the Kingdom. As the partnership expands across assets and regions, both firms plan to develop AI-enabled solutions that improve decision-making, enhance asset reliability and reduce carbon emissions through greater energy efficiency and smarter industrial operations.
GoTrust adds AI capabilities to data security platform
Privacy, security, and governance platform GoTrust has enhanced its Data Discovery & Smart Classification Solution with artificial intelligence capabilities to help enterprises identify, classify and manage sensitive data more efficiently. The upgraded solution supports over 30 enterprise connectors spanning databases, cloud platforms, CRM systems, data lakes and machine learning environments, enabling organisations to maintain a unified view of sensitive information. GoTrust said the AI-powered platform uses machine learning and natural language processing to identify personal, financial, health and biometric data while reducing manual effort and compliance costs. The enhancements are designed to help enterprises strengthen data security and comply with regulations such as India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDPA), GDPR and other global privacy frameworks.
Smartworks posts 44% revenue growth in Q1 FY27
Managed office space provider Smartworks Coworking Spaces reported a 44% year-on-year increase in revenue from operations to ₹546 crore for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, while normalised EBITDA rose 74% to ₹107 crore. Normalised profit after tax nearly tripled to ₹39 crore from ₹13 crore a year earlier, while reported PAT stood at ₹13 crore. The company said it recorded its fifth consecutive quarter of sequential revenue growth since listing, with EBITDA margin improving to 19.6%. Annualised normalised return on capital employed rose to 21.5% despite higher investment capex. Smartworks reiterated its FY27 guidance of 28-30% revenue growth, 19-20% EBITDA margin and an operational footprint of 12.5-13 million sq. ft. by March 2027.
Merlinhawk Aerospace partners with Boeing India Defence
Bengaluru-based Merlinhawk Aerospace has signed a strategic agreement with Boeing India Defence to provide in-country sustainment support for advanced Electro-Optical/Infrared (EO/IR) systems deployed on defence platforms in India. Under the partnership, Merlinhawk will leverage its L3Harris WESCAM Authorized Service Centre in Bengaluru to deliver maintenance, repair, technical support and lifecycle sustainment services. The collaboration aims to reduce turnaround times, improve operational availability and strengthen mission readiness for Indian defence customers. Merlinhawk said its dedicated WESCAM service centre is equipped with certified technical personnel, specialised tooling, OEM-approved processes and field support capabilities, enabling comprehensive local support for advanced airborne mission systems used by defence platforms.
Procol appoints Shaivya Gupta as Chief Marketing Officer
Agentic AI platform Procol has appointed Shaivya Gupta as its Chief Marketing Officer to lead global marketing, brand and communications. Gupta will focus on strengthening Procol's market positioning, customer engagement and category leadership while supporting expansion into international markets, particularly the United States. The appointment comes as the procurement and finance technology company targets 300% growth over the next year after expanding fivefold during the past two years. Procol said its growth strategy will be driven by increasing enterprise adoption in India and the US, supported by investments in customer success, strategic partnerships and demand generation initiatives aimed at strengthening its presence in key enterprise markets.
VNR VJIET secures patent for AI-based crop disease detection system
Hyderabad's VNR Vignana Jyothi Institute of Engineering & Technology has received an Indian patent for an AI-powered crop disease detection system that uses Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identify diseases in plant leaves. Developed by a multidisciplinary faculty team, the technology enables early detection of crop diseases with an accuracy of 97.7%, allowing farmers to take timely corrective action and minimise crop losses. The system analyses leaf images and recommends suitable pesticide-based remedies, supporting precision agriculture and improving productivity. The institute said the innovation addresses delayed disease identification, a major challenge affecting crop quality, yield and overall farm output across agricultural regions.
NABARD, MAHAPREIT sign MoU for green rural infrastructure
NABARD and Mahatma Phule Renewable Energy and Infrastructure Technology Ltd (MAHAPREIT) have signed a memorandum of understanding to promote climate-resilient and sustainable infrastructure across rural India, with an initial focus on Maharashtra. The partnership will finance projects in green energy, decarbonisation of government buildings, gram panchayat infrastructure, water pumping schemes and renewable energy deployment in educational and healthcare institutions.
The collaboration also aims to support biogas generation, biomass utilisation and solar-powered micro cold storage facilities, creating additional income opportunities for farmers while promoting the circular economy. The organisations said the initiative combines NABARD's expertise in rural finance with MAHAPREIT's experience in climate-focused infrastructure development.
Benevolve launches AI-powered workforce skills platform MOSAIX
Benevolve has launched MOSAIX, a cloud-based self-service workforce intelligence platform designed to help organisations manage workforce transformation through skills intelligence, workforce planning and talent development. The platform enables businesses to assess workforce capabilities, identify future skill requirements and deliver personalised learning pathways aligned with evolving business priorities.
MOSAIX integrates skills intelligence, organisational design and workforce planning into a single platform and includes an AI-powered Skill Framework Builder that allows companies to create and update role-based skills frameworks. Benevolve said the platform combines AI-enabled assessments with workforce insights to help enterprises make informed talent decisions and build agile, future-ready organisations.
(This article will be updated with the latest news throughout the day.)

articles.title: AWS Billing Bug Shows Customers Trillion-Dollar Estimates While Its Own Cost Alarms Fail to Act
articles.text:
AWS customers around the world opened their consoles on July 17 to estimated bills in the millions, billions, and in some cases trillions of dollars. One account with normal usage under $5 per month showed a $1.7 billion estimate. A Reddit user posted a screenshot showing $225,579,210,164.83. Another dashboard claimed $7.1 trillion in month-to-date charges, more than twice Amazon's market capitalization. The figures were wrong. Actual invoices were never affected. But the incident ran for more than 24 hours, and the way it unfolded says more about cloud cost management than the absurd numbers do.
(Source: Reddit AWS thread)
According to the AWS Health Dashboard, the problem began on July 16 at 7:46 PM PDT, when a configuration change in the bill computation system introduced a unit pricing error into the estimated billing pipeline. What happened next is the part practitioners should read twice. In AWS's own words:
On July 16 at 7:46 PM PDT, our alarms detected cost anomalies but failed to halt the estimated bill generation process or alert our engineering teams. We were alerted to this issue on July 17 at 12:19 AM PDT by customer escalations, and immediately began to investigate.
So the alarms went off, yet the pipeline kept generating bills and no engineer got paged. Customer escalations reached AWS at 12:19 AM, four and a half hours after its own detection fired, which means the company found out its billing system was broken because customers told it so. That is exactly how most teams discover runaway spend on AWS, except this time the roles were reversed.
The probable mechanism behind the "unit pricing" root cause is familiar to at least one engineer who has shipped this exact class of bug. One commenter on Hacker News, describing firsthand experience at AWS, explained how the billing pipeline joins metering data to pricing plans:
I've dealt with this error at AWS. It's a unit error. In my case we meant to charge like 5¢/GB, but missed the unit (GB), and then the billing system defaults to bytes. 5¢ per Byte of data transferred meant some customers were seeing MM bills within hours. Got paged by support around 2am, had it fixed and amendments issued by 3-4am, apology emails shortly after.
Services emit metering values with no prices attached, the commenter explained; every line item is defined in a pricing plan with a unit type, and a wrong unit type breaks the conversion. The contrast with this incident sits in the timestamps: that earlier bug went from page to fix in roughly two hours, while this one ran four and a half hours before customer escalations reached AWS engineers at all.
Another commenter offered a structural explanation for why testing misses this class of failure:
There will have been tests, but there will have been missing end-to-end tests. Test 1 will verify that the new system emits billing entries in some expected way. Test 2 will be in the billing system. But they won't test the two things together because it will be harder to do and the teams will have different management chains. Seen it happen several times at several companies.
The mitigation compounded the irony. After a rollback of the configuration change failed to resolve the issue, AWS paused estimated bill generation at 8:24 AM PDT, freezing the inflated numbers in place, and turned off budget and cost anomaly alerts as a precautionary measure. For the duration, the two mechanisms AWS recommends as the safety net for cost control were disabled platform-wide. Any team that wires automated responses to those alerts, from Slack escalations to SCP attachment to workload shutdown, was either triggered by phantom data before the pause or blind after it.
The Hacker News thread opened with the account holder facing the $1.7 billion estimate:
Normal usage is < $5. Obvs have created an urgent AWS support ticket. Anyone else seeing something like this.
Corey Quinn, chief cloud economist at The Duckbill Group, put the scale in perspective on LinkedIn:
I've negotiated tens of billions in AWS contracts, and I have never once gotten a customer to a trillion. The Cost Explorer team did it overnight to thousands of accounts at once.
Quinn also named the operational bind the incident created for cost teams:
Spare a thought for every FinOps practitioner who got an anomaly alert last night reading '+55,000,000,000% over baseline' and had to decide whether that was a glitch or just us-east-1 doing something new.
For some customers, the damage went beyond a bad morning. Piet van Dongen, a software architecture consultant at OpenValue, described believing the numbers long enough to act on them:
I got the email notification for a budget overrun alert and then Cost Explorer showing $369,188,086.24 in S3 costs for my personal project. I honestly thought that it was real for a full 10 minutes, I even put in a support case. I removed all my workloads for now, and I don't think I will return.
Daniel Blumenthal, a software engineering leader, connected his $843 billion estimate to a gap AWS customers have raised for a decade:
I thought my account had been hacked. Felt like I was having a heart attack. The fact that you can set alerts but can't put hard limits on your account is incredibly scary.
The longer-term worry surfaced in the same thread goes beyond the scare itself. As one commenter put it: "If AWS can goof in a way that causes obviously massive bills, what's to say they can't goof in more subtle ways and start charging small additional amounts that many people may not notice and just pay it." Absurd estimates announce themselves. Plausible ones do not.
The timing lands awkwardly for anyone following the cloud cost conversation. InfoQ covered the pattern days before the incident: practitioners documenting how AWS billing data lags roughly 24 hours behind actual spend, how budget actions evaluate against that delayed data, and how detection in real incidents came from the credit card rather than from AWS. The billing estimate incident inverts the failure. This time the data was fast and wrong instead of slow and right, but the structural lesson is identical. Billing telemetry is a dependency with its own failure modes, and automated cost controls inherit every one of them.
AWS resolved the issue and confirmed that displayed estimates never reflected actual charges. The company has not published a detailed postmortem beyond the Health Dashboard timeline, and has not said whether the alarm-to-action gap, the failed rollback, or the decision to disable budget alerts platform-wide will produce changes to the billing pipeline's own guardrails. For a system whose job is to warn everyone else about anomalous spend, the open question is who warns it.

articles.title: Google transforme son moteur de recherche en France : voici les Aperçus IA et le Mode IA
articles.text:
Attendu depuis son lancement mondial en mai 2024, le déploiement des réponses générées par intelligence artificielle de Google arrive enfin dans l’Hexagone. Après plusieurs années d’attente liées au cadre réglementaire français sur les droits voisins (une loi de 2019 imposant des négociations de rémunération avec les éditeurs de presse), la firme de Mountain View dit avoir débloqué la situation. Les utilisateurs français vont ainsi avoir accès à une nouvelle interface qui donne des réponses directes au lieu de simplement renvoyer vers des sites web.
Les réponses directement dans le moteur de recherche avec les Aperçus IA
Annoncés à l’origine en 2024, les Aperçus IA (AI Overviews) se présentent sous la forme de réponses qui s’affichent désormais directement tout en haut de la page après avoir fait votre recherche. L’algorithme de Google génère automatiquement un résumé structuré des résultats qu’il a trouvé sur le web (à condition que Google juge cette réponse utile), avant même d’afficher des liens vers les sites web sources. Comme toujours avec Google, le but est de vous donner la réponse le plus rapidement possible sans jamais quitter son écosystème.
C’est un changement très important pour les utilisateurs du moteur de recherche, mais aussi et surtout pour les éditeurs de contenus qui alimentent ces algorithmes. Pour calmer la gronde, des droits voisins ont été négociés avec les propriétaires de sites qui peuvent faire jouer une option d’opt-out via la Search Console, un réglage qui permet de désactiver complètement l’intégration de leurs pages au sein des résumés générés par l’IA. Suivre la vague ou être totalement écarté d’un outil qu’énormément de monde finira par utiliser, en somme.
La navigation conversationnelle avec le Mode IA
Les Aperçus IA, parfois controversés, ne sont pas la seule nouveauté, Google introduit également le Mode IA (AI Mode), une fonction conversationnelle directement intégrée à la recherche. Alimentée par Gemini 3.5, cette interface permet d’interagir par écrit, par la voix ou via des images tout en utilisant les capacités de raisonnement approfondies et les liens vers le web.
Mais contrairement à une conversation classique avec Gemini, ce Mode IA s’appuie de manière plus importante sur la recherche web en renvoyant vers du contenu Google Images, Google Shopping ou Google Actualités. L’utilisateur a ensuite la possibilité de poser des questions complémentaires directement depuis un Aperçu IA, pour avoir une discussion plus interactive avec l’IA. Les Aperçus IA et le Mode IA sont disponibles depuis ce matin, mercredi 22 juillet à 7h00.
👉🏻 Suivez l’actualité tech en temps réel : ajoutez 01net à vos sources sur Google, et abonnez-vous à notre canal WhatsApp.
Source : Google

articles.title: VLC media player : télécharger le lecteur vidéo gratuit sans risque
articles.text:
VLC media player : télécharger le lecteur vidéo gratuit sans risque
Le guide pour installer le lecteur de VideoLAN en toute sécurité, sans tomber sur un site frauduleux.
VLC media player fait partie de ces logiciels que beaucoup installent presque par réflexe. Gratuit, open source et porté par le projet VideoLAN, il lit la plupart des fichiers vidéo et audio sans réclamer de pack de codecs supplémentaire. MP4, MKV, AVI, fichiers audio, DVD, sous-titres, flux réseau : le lecteur s’adapte à des usages très différents, sur Windows, macOS, Linux, Android ou iOS.
Cette popularité a aussi attiré les faux sites de téléchargement. Certains reprennent le nom VLC pour pousser des installateurs modifiés, des publicités trompeuses ou des logiciels indésirables. Pour récupérer VLC media player sans prendre de risque, la bonne source compte donc autant que le logiciel lui-même.
Le top 4 des solutions de sécurité
Qu’est-ce que VLC media player ?
VLC media player est un lecteur multimédia gratuit, libre et open source. Son intérêt principal tient en une idée simple : ouvrir une grande variété de fichiers sans demander à l’utilisateur d’installer des codecs supplémentaires. C’est ce qui explique son succès, notamment auprès de ceux qui récupèrent des vidéos dans différents formats ou qui veulent éviter les lecteurs trop limités.
Le logiciel prend en charge de nombreux formats vidéo et audio, dont MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, MPEG, MP3 ou AAC. Il peut aussi lire des DVD, des CD audio, des VCD, des sous-titres séparés et certains flux réseau. Sur ordinateur comme sur mobile, VLC reste surtout apprécié pour sa simplicité : on installe, on ouvre le fichier, et la lecture démarre dans la plupart des cas.
Autre point important : VLC n’appartient pas à une grande plateforme commerciale. Le lecteur est développé par VideoLAN, un projet open source connu pour son approche sobre, sans publicité invasive et sans ajout de composants inutiles. Cette philosophie participe largement à la confiance dont bénéficie le logiciel depuis des années.
Ce que VLC media player permet de faire au quotidien
Pour un usage simple, VLC sert d’abord à lire une vidéo ou un fichier audio sans se poser trop de questions. Mais le lecteur va plus loin : il peut gérer des sous-titres, changer de piste audio, ajuster le décalage entre le son et l’image, ouvrir une liste de lecture ou lire un flux réseau.
C’est aussi un outil pratique lorsque le lecteur intégré à Windows, macOS, Android ou iOS refuse d’ouvrir un fichier. VLC accepte de nombreux formats et garde une interface assez sobre, même si ses réglages avancés permettent d’aller beaucoup plus loin pour ceux qui en ont besoin.
Les utilisateurs plus avancés peuvent également s’en servir pour convertir certains fichiers, lire des médias depuis une adresse réseau ou tester différents flux de streaming. Ce n’est pas seulement un lecteur vidéo : c’est un logiciel multimédia polyvalent, capable de rendre service dans des situations très variées.
Où télécharger VLC media player sans risque ?
La source la plus sûre pour télécharger VLC media player reste le site officiel du projet VideoLAN. Sur Windows et macOS, il permet de récupérer la version adaptée à son système, notamment en 64 bits lorsque l’appareil le prend en charge. Sur Linux, VLC peut aussi être installé depuis les dépôts officiels de la distribution utilisée, ce qui permet de passer par un canal contrôlé par l’écosystème du système d’exploitation.
Sur mobile, la règle est la même : mieux vaut passer par les boutiques officielles. Un appareil Android doit utiliser Google Play, tandis qu’un iPhone ou un iPad doit récupérer VLC depuis l’App Store. Ces plateformes ne suppriment pas tous les risques, mais elles réduisent fortement la probabilité d’installer une application modifiée.
Avant de cliquer sur un bouton de téléchargement, prenez quelques secondes pour vérifier l’adresse du site. Le domaine de VideoLAN doit apparaître clairement, sans faute d’orthographe, extension suspecte ou redirection vers une page qui multiplie les boutons “Download”. C’est souvent là que les pièges commencent.
Pourquoi faut-il se méfier des faux téléchargements VLC ?
La popularité de VLC media player en fait une cible facile pour les sites frauduleux. Beaucoup d’utilisateurs cherchent simplement un lecteur gratuit pour ouvrir une vidéo, sans forcément vérifier la source du fichier. Les pages douteuses exploitent ce réflexe en affichant de gros boutons de téléchargement, parfois accompagnés de publicités qui imitent l’apparence d’un site officiel.
Le risque le plus fréquent concerne les installateurs modifiés. Il ne s’agit pas toujours d’un faux VLC visible au premier regard. Le fichier peut ressembler à un installateur classique, mais ajouter en arrière-plan un logiciel publicitaire, une extension de navigateur ou un outil qui change le moteur de recherche par défaut. Le lecteur recherché peut même s’installer correctement, ce qui rend le piège moins évident.
Les liens sponsorisés méritent aussi un minimum de prudence. Lorsqu’un utilisateur tape “télécharger VLC media player” dans un moteur de recherche, les premiers résultats peuvent parfois être des annonces. Certaines sont légitimes, d’autres renvoient vers des sites tiers dont l’origine du fichier n’est pas toujours claire. Pour un logiciel aussi connu que VLC, mieux vaut éviter les détours inutiles et passer directement par VideoLAN ou par une boutique officielle.
Comment reconnaître un faux site VLC ?
Un faux site VLC cherche souvent à copier les codes du vrai : nom du logiciel bien visible, icône proche du cône orange, gros bouton de téléchargement, promesse de version gratuite. Le détail qui trahit le piège se trouve souvent dans l’adresse web. Une lettre changée, un nom de domaine inhabituel ou une redirection vers une page trop chargée en publicités doivent alerter.
Autre indice : la présence de plusieurs boutons “Télécharger” sur la même page. Un site sérieux n’a pas besoin de multiplier les boutons concurrents ni de pousser des logiciels annexes. Un fichier VLC officiel ne doit pas vous imposer une barre d’outils, une extension de navigateur, un moteur de recherche ou un programme tiers sans rapport avec le lecteur multimédia.
Avant d’installer, il faut donc vérifier trois choses : l’adresse du site, le nom du fichier récupéré et les étapes proposées pendant l’installation. Si une case précochée ajoute un logiciel inconnu, si l’installateur propose un “pack recommandé” ou si la page semble insister lourdement sur des offres annexes, mieux vaut abandonner et repartir depuis la source officielle.
Un antivirus est-il utile pour télécharger VLC media player ?
Le danger ne vient pas de VLC lui-même lorsqu’il est téléchargé depuis VideoLAN ou depuis une boutique officielle. Le vrai risque se situe avant : un faux bouton « Télécharger », une publicité sponsorisée trompeuse, un site qui copie l’apparence du projet VideoLAN ou un installateur modifié qui ajoute des logiciels indésirables.
Dans ce contexte, un antivirus sert surtout de filet de sécurité. Il peut bloquer une page suspecte, analyser le fichier récupéré et repérer un programme ajouté discrètement à l’installation. Avast peut suffire pour une protection accessible sur PC, Norton 360 ajoute des fonctions de sécurité web plus larges, Surfshark One associe antivirus, VPN et outils de confidentialité, tandis que Bitdefender reste une solution solide pour détecter les malwares sur plusieurs appareils.
Le bon réflexe reste le même : télécharger VLC media player depuis la source officielle, puis vérifier le fichier si un doute subsiste. Un antivirus ne remplace pas la vigilance, mais il limite les dégâts en cas de mauvais clic, surtout lorsque l’on passe par un lien sponsorisé ou une page de téléchargement douteuse.
Les bons réflexes après installation
Une fois VLC installé, le premier réflexe consiste à vérifier que le logiciel reste à jour. Les mises à jour ne servent pas seulement à ajouter des fonctions : elles corrigent aussi des bugs, améliorent la stabilité et renforcent parfois la compatibilité avec certains formats audio ou vidéo.
Vous pouvez ensuite associer VLC à certains types de fichiers pour l’utiliser comme lecteur par défaut. Sur Windows, macOS ou Linux, cette option permet d’ouvrir plus facilement les fichiers MP4, MKV, AVI, MPEG, MP3 ou AAC depuis l’explorateur de fichiers. Ce réglage n’a rien d’obligatoire, mais il évite de devoir choisir le lecteur à chaque ouverture.
Pour les sous-titres, VLC offre aussi quelques réglages utiles. Il permet d’ajouter un fichier de sous-titres séparé, de changer de piste audio, d’ajuster le décalage entre le son et l’image ou de modifier l’affichage du texte à l’écran. Ces fonctions sont pratiques pour les vidéos en version originale, les fichiers récupérés avec plusieurs pistes ou les contenus dont la synchronisation n’est pas parfaite.
Enfin, évitez les mises à jour proposées par des sites tiers. Pour rester du côté sûr, passez par VLC lui-même, par le site officiel de VideoLAN, par les dépôts officiels de votre distribution Linux ou par les boutiques d’applications reconnues sur Android et iOS.
VLC media player ou un autre lecteur vidéo ?
VLC media player reste une valeur sûre pour lire des vidéos, de la musique, des sous-titres ou des flux réseau sans multiplier les logiciels. D’autres lecteurs existent, comme Media Player Classic ou les lecteurs intégrés à Windows, macOS, Android et iOS, mais peu offrent le même équilibre entre simplicité, compatibilité et gratuité.
Le choix dépend surtout de vos usages. Pour ouvrir rapidement un fichier courant, le lecteur intégré à votre système peut suffire. Pour lire des formats plus variés, gérer des sous-titres, ouvrir un fichier récalcitrant ou utiliser un lecteur multimédia vraiment polyvalent, VLC reste difficile à remplacer.
Le point à surveiller n’est donc pas VLC, mais l’endroit où vous le téléchargez. En passant par VideoLAN, les dépôts officiels Linux ou les boutiques d’applications reconnues, vous évitez l’essentiel des pièges. Une protection antivirus active ajoute une sécurité utile, surtout si vous avez cliqué sur un lien sponsorisé ou une page de téléchargement douteuse.

articles.title: We take a hands on look at the new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Tech Guide has taken a first hands-on look at the brand new Galaxy Z Fold 8 – the newest member of Samsung’s foldable range.
The device has a brand new shape and its own look and feel, which will be attractive to customers who are considering their first foldable smartphone.
With its shorter and wider 5.5-inch front screen and useful 7.6-inch inside display, the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 could very well be the on-ramp to the foldable category for many new customers.
For us one of the complaints we’ve always had about the Fold devices over the years was the narrow front screen that made it difficult for us to type out our messages.
But the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has solved that problem with its wider front screen that offers enough room for even our fat thumbs to comfortably write our messages.
The 5.5-inch display was also big enough to scroll social media and even browse the web.
But what sold us was the inside 7.6-inch display with its 4:3 aspect ratio.
This wider shape means it can be used in two ways.
In landscape it’s ideal for watching content like YouTube and your streaming services.
You can also run apps side by side.
But when you turn it around into portrait mode, it’s the precise shape of an e-reader and a tablet which makes it perfect for reading, browsing the web and scrolling social media.
The advantage it has over the Fold8 Ultra, despite it having a slightly smaller display, is the fact that it has these two distinct modes.
The Fold8 Ultra might have a larger 8-inch display but it has a square shape which means so no matter how you hold the device it’s going to look the same.
The new Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 is a lot more approachable, especially for customers who may have thought the previous Samsung foldables were too much phone or too big and bulky.
We think the Galaxy Z Fold 8 will be a popular product in the lineup but the Galaxy Z Fold8 Ultra, which is a noticeable improvement over the Galaxy Z Fold7, will still attract the already growing number of foldable users.
Last year Samsung said the Galaxy Z Fold7 enjoyed a 48 per cent growth over the Fold6 with 62 per cent new to foldables.
Since 2021 the Samsung foldable user base has tripled.
But we need to address the elephant in the room.
And that’s the fact that Apple’s rumoured foldable iPhone will also likely adopt a similar passport shape that Samsung has just released.
We suspect Apple’s entry into the foldable market will not only validate the whole category but also help Samsung sell even more foldable devices.
Apple releasing its first foldable iPhone will no doubt have a seismic effect on the category.
But a rising tide lifts all boats and Samsung will no doubt win new customers especially those loyal Android users who see the foldable iPhone and want the Android alternative, which will be the Galaxy Z Fold8.
* Stephen Fenech travelled to London as a guest of Samsung

articles.title: Les députés européens utilisent de plus en plus l'IA... alors le Parlement crée sa plateforme interne
articles.text:
L'intelligence artificielle est un souci partout, et ce, jusqu'aux plus hautes sphères du pouvoir. Le Parlement européen prend ainsi des mesures pour tenter de réguler la technologie en son sein.
On prend de plus en plus la question de l'intelligence artificielle au sérieux au niveau européen. On sait ainsi que la Commission européenne est à l'origine d'un nouveau projet pour mettre au monde un modèle IA open source frontière couvrant les 24 langues de l'Union. Et si l'UE veut rivaliser à l'extérieur avec la Chine et les États-Unis, elle veut aussi mieux réguler ce qui se passe à l'intérieur de ses institutions.
Le Parlement européen de plus en plus inquiets de lutilisation de l'IA par les députés
De nombreux salariés utilisent l'intelligence artificielle comme un assistant au quotidien de leur travail. Et ils ne sont pas les seuls, puisque cette habitude se retrouve dorénavant aussi de plus en plus au Parlement européen, où les députés en font un large usage pour produire des amendements et achever leurs travaux législatifs, selon Politico.
L'usage est tel que lors d'une réunion tenue au mois de juillet dernier, des présidents de commission ont partagé leur inquiétude sur cette utilisation. « Le Parlement n'a pas été épargné par les erreurs liées à l'IA et les contenus trompeurs générés par IA » fait remarquer le député européen du groupe des Socialistes et démocrates, Brando Benifei.
La nouvelle plateforme EPGenAI Hub, la solution ?
Au sein du Parlement européen, près de 2 100 personnes font un usage quotidien de l'IA générative (ce qui représente un cinquième des effectifs). L'inquiétude des autorités porte autant sur la qualité du travail produit quand il est assisté par l'IA que sur le partage de documents parlementaires avec des plateformes d'acteurs privés, qui ne sont pas contrôlés par Bruxelles.
Comprenant qu'il ne peut pas tout simplement interdire l'usage de l'IA, le Parlement européen a mis au monde sa propre plateforme, baptisée EPGenAI Hub. Cette dernière a déjà été présentée aux députés ainsi qu'à leurs assistants. Reste que, même via cette plateforme, les députés peuvent autant utiliser des modèles exploités localement (comme GPT-OSS, Mistral Small ou Llama) dans des infrastructures sécurisées par le Parlement européen, que des modèles hébergés à l'extérieur. Parmi ces derniers, on retrouve notamment ChatGPT ou bien Claude Sonnet. Soit une ouverture à l'offre américaine, avec tous les risques que cela peut entraîner.
Conscient des critiques qui peuvent encore être faites, le Parlement européen a tenu à expliquer que rien n'était encore figé. « L'offre de modèles est en train d'être réexaminée, notamment compte tenu de la disponibilité de modèles open source et de modèles souverains de l'UE proposés par des fournisseurs de cloud souverain qui ont récemment signé un contrat avec la Commission européenne » a précisé le service presse du Parlement.

articles.title: Palo Alto Networks to Acquire Observability Platform Provider Embrace
articles.text:
Palo Alto Networks (NASDAQ: PANW) on Tuesday announced its intent to acquire Embrace, a provider of user-focused observability, in a move to add Real User Monitoring (RUM) capabilities to its Observability platform. Financial terms of the deal were not disclosed.
Alongside the acquisition, the company introduced Synthetics, a new capability developed in-house by its Autonomous Digital Experience Management (ADEM) team for proactively validating application performance from locations around the globe. Together, the additions extend Palo Alto Networks’ Observability platform into Digital Experience Monitoring, giving customers a unified view spanning end-user interactions, application validation, and backend infrastructure.
According to the company, Embrace’s RUM technology is built for modern, cloud-native environments, while Synthetics leverages Palo Alto Networks’ globally distributed infrastructure to validate application availability before problems reach users.
“To truly understand how their applications are performing, organizations need to see the whole picture — from the moment a user taps or clicks to what exactly happens on the backend,” said Lee Klarich, Chief Product & Technology Officer at Palo Alto Networks. He added that linking the capabilities with the company’s Cortex AgentiX would allow organizations to both detect and automatically remediate issues.
The deal builds on Palo Alto Networks’ January 2026 $3.35 billion acquisition of Chronosphere, part of a broader observability push that the company says has surpassed $300 million in annual recurring revenue.
The acquisition is subject to customary closing conditions and is expected to close in the first quarter of Palo Alto Networks’ fiscal 2027.

articles.title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra vs Galaxy Z Fold 7 : tout ce que Samsung a changé sur son pliable ultra haut de gamme
articles.text:
Sur la photo, difficile de les distinguer. Même gabarit, même poids au gramme près, mêmes tailles d’écran. Pourtant, le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra ne se contente pas de reprendre le flambeau du Galaxy Z Fold 7 : il se veut l’équivalent pliable du S26 Ultra et bombe ses caractéristiques quitte à faire grimper l’addition. Samsung l’a dévoilé aux côtés du Fold 8 et du Flip 8.
La base ne bouge pas : écran externe de 6,5 pouces, dalle interne de 8,0 pouces une fois dépliée, et toujours ce refus obstiné du stylet S Pen, comme sur le Fold 7. Samsung a concentré ses efforts sur trois postes : batterie, appareil photo et écran. Le reste relève de l’ajustement. Petit avertissement au passage, entre Fold 8, Fold 8 Ultra et Flip 8, la nouvelle nomenclature a de quoi perdre du monde.
Toutes les annonces de Samsung lors de cette Galaxy Unpacked
La conférence estivale Galaxy Unpacked de Samsung, le constructeur dévoile ses derniers produits en date. Pour suivre la conférence direct, nous vous invitons à suivre notre live écrit.
La conférence de Samsung a lieu ce mercredi 22 juillet depuis 15h.
Pour les smartphones pliables de la marque, ce sont bien trois modèles qui sont dévoilés par le constructeur : le Galaxy Z Fold 8, le Galaxy Z Flip 8 et Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Vous êtes perdus dans la nouvelle gamme ? Pas de soucis, nous avons défriché les produits tout juste sortis et avons distingué leurs différences.
A cette occasion, nous avons pu prendre en main le Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra. Sur cette nouvelle gamme, Samsung intègre enfin une batterie silicium-carbone, voici les explications techniques de la marque. Encore une fois, Samsung réalise des prouesses sur son écran. Enfin nous avons fait un comparatif du Z Fold 8 face à notre maquette en impression 3D du futur iPhone pliant.
Du côté des montres connectées, Samsung dévoile deux nouveaux produits : la Samsung Galaxy Watch 9 ainsi que la Galaxy Watch Ultra 2. Notre collègue journaliste Geoffroy a eu l’occasion de tester la Samsung Galaxy Watch 2 Ultra. Vous pouvez aussi lire notre prise en main de la Galaxy Watch 9.
Notre vidéo récapitulative des annonces Samsung
Une batterie au silicium-carbone !
Commençons par la vraie surprise. Pour la première fois, Samsung glisse une batterie au silicium-carbone dans l’un de ses smartphones. Cette technologie loge plus de capacité dans le même volume, sans faire gonfler l’épaisseur. La capacité passe donc à 5 000 mAh, contre 4 400 mAh sur le Fold 7. Soit 600 mAh de rab, de quoi grimper de 24 à 27 heures de lecture vidéo d’après Samsung. Trois heures de gagnées, si c’est vrai, c’est un vrai plus pour ce pliable réputé pour son autonomie fragile.
L’ultra grand-angle du Galaxy S26 Ultra
Côté photo, le duo de tête ne bouge quasiment pas : capteur principal de 200 mégapixels et téléobjectif x3 de 10 mégapixels, identiques d’un modèle à l’autre. C’est l’ultra grand-angle qui prend un coup de fouet. On passe d’un modeste 12 mégapixels (f/2.2) à un capteur de 50 mégapixels ouvrant à f/1.9, celui-là même que l’on trouve sur le Galaxy S26 Ultra.
Ce nouveau module laisse entrer 34 % de lumière en plus, promet des clichés de nuit plus propres et débloque la vidéo 8K sur cet objectif. Sur le Fold 7, l’ultra grand-angle faisait figure de parent pauvre. Cette fois, il tient enfin son rang, au moins sur le papier.
Le HONOR Magic V6 repousse les limites du smartphone pliable avec un design distinctif et robuste, des performances photo de haut niveau et une batterie généreuse conçue pour durer.
Plus fin et plus résistant
Déplié, le Fold 8 Ultra gagne 0,1 mm de finesse (4,1 mm contre 4,2 mm), une différence qu’on ne sentira jamais sous les doigts. Plié, l’épaisseur ne change pas (8,9 mm).
On conserve le châssis en Aluminium Armor du Fold 7, mais la charnière Armor FlexHinge adopte un mécanisme à friction réduite. Idem pour l’écran avant qui se pare d’un nouveau verre Corning Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3. En revanche, on conserve le Gorilla Victus 2 à l’arrière.
En outre, l’écran interne évolue grandement avec l’adjonction de composants en titane dans la dalle. Cette technologie nommée Flex Titanium est censée proposer une dalle à la fois plus fine et plus résistante et aussi réduire encore la pliure.
Plus lumineux
Les écrans gardent leurs diagonales mais gagne en luminosité, avec un pic à 3 000 nits contre 2 600 nits promis sur le Fold 7, soit 15 % de mieux face au soleil.
Plus puissant
À l’intérieur, le Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy remplace le Snapdragon 8 Elite for Galaxy, soit une génération de gagnée sur la puce et toujours un SoC légèrement surcadencé. Reste à voir si le système de refroidissement a été suffisament optimisé. L’espace est limité pour la chambre à vapeur et d’expérience, la dernière grosse puce de Qualcomm a tendance à chauffer.
Le Fold 8 Ultra démarre aussi directement sous Android 17 et la surcouche One UI 9, là où le Fold 7 était livré sous Android 16 (One UI 8). Une fonction Galaxy AI inédite sur les Z débarque. Il s’agit de Now Nudge. Héritée des S26, elle jongle avec vos rappels et recommandations selon le contexte, proposant notamment d’afficher le calendrier en multiécran si vous avez une date dans un message.
Et plus cher
Parlons tarif. Le Fold 8 Ultra démarre à 2 299 euros en 256 Go, passe à 2 399 euros en 512 Go et culmine à 2 599 euros en 1 To. Le Fold 7 ouvrait le bal à 2 099 euros pour grimper jusqu’à 2 519 euros. On est à 200 euros de plus sur l’entrée de gamme.
Et ne comptez pas sur l’offre de précommande habituelle. Samsung a tué son cadeau sur le stockage. On ne peut pas bénéficier du stockage supérieur pour le prix de l’inférieur. Désormais, c’est 100 euros de réduction pour un 512 Go au lieu d’un 256 Go et 200 euros pour un 1 To au lieu d’un 512 Go. Au bilan, il reste à charge 100 ou 200 euros pour passer au stockage supérieur.
La palette de couleurs change aussi du tout au tout : exit le Bleu Nuit et le Vert d’eau, place au Techno Violet, Graphite, Blanc et Techno Vert.
Faut-il sauter le pas depuis un Fold 7 ?
Que nenni : 0,1 mm, 600 mAh et un meilleur ultra grand-angle ne valent pas 2 300 euros de rachat. Pour qui vient d’un modèle plus ancien ou découvre le pliable, en revanche, le Fold 8 Ultra est la version la plus aboutie du grand format de Samsung.

articles.title: Ne ratez pas la conférence Samsung cet après-midi : des nouveaux téléphones arrivent
articles.text:
Jour de conférence pour Samsung. Une fois n’est pas coutume, la marque a choisi l’Europe pour son rendez-vous d’été : deux ans après un passage à Paris à l’occasion des JO de 2024, le constructeur coréen est revenu sur le Vieux Continent, cette fois à Londres. Numerama est sur place pour essayer les produits (et vous les ramener en test).
L’enjeu est double pour Samsung. D’un côté, rattraper les constructeurs chinois, qui l’avaient distancé sur la batterie et la recharge. De l’autre, prendre les devants avant l’arrivée du premier iPhone pliant d’Apple, attendu pour la fin de l’année 2026. Résultat : une génération bien plus riche en nouveautés que ce que les rumeurs annonçaient, avec un nouveau format passeport, une première batterie silicium-carbone et un écran repensé.
Notre vidéo sur le Samsung Galaxy Unpacked
Le résumé des annonces Samsung
Samsung a présenté cinq produits : trois smartphones pliants et deux montres connectées. Voici l’essentiel à retenir sur chacun.
Galaxy Z Fold 8
C’est la vraie nouveauté de la conférence. Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 adopte un format passeport : plus court, plus large et presque carré une fois ouvert. Son écran externe de 5,5 pouces en 10:16 se manipule comme un smartphone classique, et sa dalle interne de 7,6 pouces bascule en 4:3. Avec 201 grammes sur la balance, c’est le Fold le plus léger jamais fait par Samsung. Il embarque une batterie silicium-carbone de 4 800 mAh, mais se contente de deux capteurs photo. Prix de départ : 1 999 euros.
Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra
Le Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra est le véritable successeur du Z Fold 7 et le pliant le plus complet de la marque. Il conserve le grand écran interne de 8 pouces presque carré, gagne un téléobjectif x3 et une batterie de 5 000 mAh qui atteint 67 % en 30 minutes. Fin de 4,1 mm une fois déplié, il profite lui aussi de l’écran Flex Titanium. Son prix démarre à 2 199 euros, soit 200 euros de plus que le Fold 8.
Galaxy Z Flip 8
Le Galaxy Z Flip 8 évolue peu, mais coûte 100 euros de plus que le Flip 7. Le clapet de Samsung mise sur le style, avec un design affiné à 180 grammes, une recharge accélérée à 45 W et une nouvelle puce Exynos 2600. Ses écrans, sa batterie de 4 300 mAh et ses appareils photo bougent peu. Prix de départ : 1 299 euros.
Galaxy Watch 9
La Galaxy Watch 9 remplace la Watch 8, toujours en deux tailles et en versions Bluetooth ou 4G. Les nouveautés portent surtout sur un boîtier affiné, un écran plus lumineux à 3 000 nits, une nouvelle puce et plusieurs indicateurs ajoutés à Samsung Health. Vendue à partir de 409 euros, elle se rapproche des tarifs d’une Apple Watch Series 11 ou d’une Pixel Watch 4.
Galaxy Watch Ultra 2
La Galaxy Watch Ultra 2 succède à la première Watch Ultra, la réponse de Samsung à l’Apple Watch Ultra. Elle garde son boîtier de 47 mm en titane et son positionnement sportif, mais corrige surtout l’autonomie avec une batterie de 800 mAh, dans un châssis un peu plus fin. Uniquement en 4G, à 749 euros, avec 60 jours de Strava offerts au lancement.

articles.title: Nvidia is giving developers more control over DLSS 5, after accusations it turns games into "AI slop"
articles.text:
What just happened? Nvidia has revealed more details about DLSS 5, which has possibly become its most hated product ever because many consider it little more than an AI filter. The company has now explained more about the latest iteration of its rendering technology, including the (just) two sliders developers can use to alter the intensity.
Nvidia used its SIGGRAPH 2026 keynote to demonstrate the controls that developers will receive when DLSS 5 launches this fall. The two main global sliders are Structure Intensity and Tone Intensity, which essentially determines how enthusiastically the AI repaints a frame.
Structure Intensity controls high-frequency details, including ambient occlusion, reflections, contact shadows, and subsurface scattering. Turning it up can improve how light passes through skin, hair, foliage, and translucent materials. Tone Intensity handles lower-frequency elements such as lighting, colors, and the broader mood of a scene.
These aren't the only controls, despite the attention-grabbing total of only two sliders. DLSS 5 currently offers three separately trained models, labeled A, B, and C, each producing a different interpretation of the same rendered image.
Developers are not locked into one model for an entire game and can swap them between scenes, environments, and cutscenes.
The system can also automatically identify and mask a character, allowing artists to apply DLSS 5 only to that person or leave them untouched while enhancing the environment. Developers can create their own engine-side masks for individual objects or groups of props, with independent Structure and Tone settings for each. Nvidia demonstrated separate controls for bottles, grapes, a pitcher, and other scene elements.
That granular masking could potentially ease some concerns about DLSS 5 turning every character into the same uncannily smooth AI creation. As reported following the technology's March unveiling, its alterations to Resident Evil Requiem's Grace Ashcroft and Leon Kennedy led to accusations of it being AI slop. Jensen Huang responded that critics were "completely wrong" and insisted developers would retain full artistic control.
Nvidia says DLSS 5 begins with the conventionally rendered frame and then adds a learned generative stage to enrich its appearance. It added that Internal buffers containing information such as albedo, surface normals, and lighting help anchor the result to the artists' intentions. Motion vectors allow the model to process frames causally – one frame in and one frame out – without looking ahead, which Nvidia says prevents shimmering, drifting, and swimming.
The company says it has distilled knowledge from much larger generative systems into a compact, one-step pixel-space diffusion transformer designed solely to improve rendered game frames. Nvidia reiterated that the finished technology is intended to run on a single GPU, although it still has not revealed performance or VRAM requirements.
Early hands-on coverage claimed that DLSS 5 was more nuanced than a simple face filter, but questions remain. Nvidia previously "confirmed" that its primary input is a 2D frame plus motion vectors, and the system can still infer details incorrectly when objects become obscured.
Nvidia says more developer controls are being built based on partner feedback. We'll find out whether the three models, object masks, and two main sliders are enough to win over gamers when DLSS 5 arrives this fall.

articles.title: Humanoid raises $152M at $1.35B valuation to bring human-like robots into factories - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Humanoid raises $152M at $1.35B valuation to bring human-like robots into factories
London-based artificial intelligence and robotics firm SKL Robotics Ltd., doing business as Humanoid, today announced it raised $152 million in funding, bringing the company’s post-money valuation to $1.35 billion.
The round was led by Prime Movers Lab, a venture capital firm focused on scientific and bleeding-edge technology startups. Investors also participating in the funding included Schaeﬄer, Bosch, Fubon Financial Holding Venture Capital and Aglaé Ventures.
“In just two years, we’ve gone from an idea to becoming Europe’s first pure-play humanoid robotics unicorn, partnered with some of the world’s leading industrial companies and built one of the strongest pipelines in the industry,” said founder and Chief Executive Artem Sokolov. “What we’ve accomplished in such a short time would typically take a decade.”
Humanoid is best known for building industrial-grade humanoid robotics platforms, including wheeled and bipedal models, both part of the HMND-01 Alpha family.
The wheeled version is designed primarily for industrial work where having a solid base benefits a robot, leaving it with a torso and arms that can interact with components, sort and move objects, and provide logistical support. The bipedal model adds legs, making it a walking robot, best for close quarters and situations where human-like movement is needed to adapt to limited-access or changing environments.
Since the company’s founding in 2024, Humanoid has scored numerous high-profile partnerships with Fortune 500 companies, including SAP SE, Nvidia Corp., Robert Bosch GmbH and Siemens AG. In May, the company signed a massive binding commercial rollout with global manufacturing company Schaeffler AG to deploy between 1,000 and 2,000 wheeled humanoid units across facilities by 2032.
“Bosch will act as Humanoid’s contract manufacturing partner, while also providing strategic consulting and technical expertise in hardware design, production, and supply chain,” said Bosch Chief Technology Officer Mathias Pillin.
Under the hood, Humanoid developed what the company calls a “shared brain” for robotic operations called KinetIQ. The company describes this system as an intelligence framework that can orchestrate the execution of multiple interrelated tasks across multiple robots in industrial and service settings. It provides everything required for robots to communicate and hand off tasks while working toward a goal.
That means a company can deploy an entire fleet of robots across a product line, each with its own individual job, which can coordinate together to complete work.
The humanoid robotics industry is experiencing a boom as big industries and startups continue to push to a future where they will be present in factories and customer service. Elon Musk’s Tesla Inc. is pushing toward deploying its Optimus humanoid robot into factories. Figure AI Inc. is actively testing its humanoids at a BMW Manufacturing plant in South Carolina. Agility Robotics Inc. is piloting its Digit robots with Amazon.com Inc. and GXO Logistics Inc., and Apptronik Inc. partnered with Mercedes-Benz to pilot its Apollo robot.
Humanoid said it will use the new funding to build towards a future where intelligent robots work safely alongside people. The company intends to develop and launch its next-generation of humanoids, push toward long-term commercial deployments, start mass manufacturing its wheel-based robots and accelerate research and development of its AI and software frameworks for general-purpose applications.

articles.title: Microsoft is building an AI stack it doesn't fully own — on purpose
articles.text:
Microsoft is building an AI stack it doesn’t fully own — on purpose
Microsoft and Mistral are deepening their partnership with a multibillion-dollar agreement focused on enterprise AI infrastructure. The goal is to give organizations more flexibility over where they run frontier models and how those deployments are managed, particularly in regions with tight data residency and sovereignty requirements.
Under the deal, announced Tuesday, Microsoft will use Mistral’s expanding European compute infrastructure to increase regional capacity. Mistral, meanwhile, plans to deploy thousands of NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPUs to power everything from model training to multi-agent workloads.
For engineering teams in regulated industries, the announcement emphasizes where enterprise AI is heading. Many organizations no longer want the public cloud to be the only place they can run AI models. They’re asking for deployments that fit into the infrastructure they already have, including on-premises and air-gapped environments.
Sovereign compute meets agentic AI
At the compute layer, the agreement gives Microsoft access to European-operated infrastructure outside its traditional first-party data centers and leased facilities. The move builds on Microsoft’s European Digital Commitments, announced in 2025, which focus on keeping customer data in Europe and helping organizations meet regional regulatory requirements.
Crucially, Mistral will power this infrastructure with NVIDIA’s next-generation Vera Rubin rack-scale platform. Because sovereign environments support multi-step agentic workflows, this hardware pairing is essential. NVIDIA claims the platform delivers up to 10x the agent throughput at scale compared to its Grace Blackwell generation.
“Europe should have access to the world’s most capable AI without compromising control over their data, operations or digital future.”
Even though exact financial terms, capacity allocations, and rollout timelines have not been made public, the agreement positions Mistral as both an AI model supplier and an independent European compute vendor for Microsoft’s enterprise ecosystem. For European companies wary of the US CLOUD Act, the appeal is obvious — though whether a US-headquartered provider can fully place data beyond its reach remains legally contested.
“Europe should have access to the world’s most capable AI without compromising control over their data, operations or digital future,” said Microsoft Vice Chair and President Brad Smith in the announcement.
The model layer
At the model and API tier, Microsoft announced that Mistral Medium 3.5 and Mistral OCR 4 are now live in Microsoft Foundry, with Medium 3.5 also integrated into Microsoft Copilot Studio.
Among the models coming to Azure AI Foundry is Mistral Medium 3.5, an open-weight model with 128 billion parameters and a 256,000-token context window, which could indicate it’s better suited for applications that need to work across large documents or extended conversations.
Microsoft is also adding Mistral OCR 4, which is designed for document-heavy AI workflows. The model can process documents in 170 languages and preserve information about page layout, including bounding boxes, document structure, and confidence levels.
The model can process documents in 170 languages and preserve information about page layout, including bounding boxes, document structure, and confidence levels
Air-gapped deployments go mainstream
For developers, the primary technical win is architectural symmetry. Engineers can build, test, and fine-tune applications inside Microsoft Foundry and migrate those workloads across public Azure, Azure Local, or sovereign infrastructure operated by Mistral without having to refactor underlying workflows.
This hybrid portability targets industries bound by strict compliance regulations. The deployment options also include fully air-gapped environments, allowing organizations to run AI workloads on networks that remain completely isolated from the public internet.
Deployment flexibility drives decisions
The partnership indicates that deployment flexibility is becoming part of the buying decision. Many organizations want the freedom to run AI in the cloud, on-premises, or in regional infrastructure without being locked into a single approach. And that’s where Microsoft’s expanded relationship with Mistral fits so well.
The companies are betting that giving customers more deployment options will weigh just as much as offering competitive models. If the strategy works, Microsoft will be providing the control plane for how the world’s most regulated industries run it.
